title: Identity Proofing
audience: Policy, legal, risk and governance leaders
learning_outcome: Evaluate identity proofing using its stated research question, evidence requirements and implementation risks.
portfolio_output: A two-page executive action brief separating known evidence, assumptions, risks and next tests.
assessment_criterion: Explain the construct; test the stated hypothesis; identify one confounder; select a valid measure; recommend an evidence-safe next action.
research_question: How can identity proofing be designed and governed so that identity, consent and authority remain accurate, understandable, revocable, contestable and aligned with the person’s actual intentions?
evidence_boundary: Working hypothesis and research material are not established findings. Unknowns include effect size, legal variation, cross-border recognition, proofing quality, accessibility, cultural expectations, adversarial adaptation, optimal assurance level and institutional adoption cost.

modules.title: Executive briefing
modules.purpose: Definition, why it matters and decision context.
modules.voice_test: Produce a clean 10-12 minute narrated lesson excerpt from the authoritative script.

modules.title: Evidence lab
modules.purpose: Research question, hypothesis, variables and evidence requirements.
modules.voice_test: Produce a 10-12 minute narrated lesson excerpt with technical terminology and lists.

modules.title: Applied scenario
modules.purpose: Evaluate risks, mitigations and stakeholder impacts in a realistic executive decision.
modules.voice_test: Produce a 10-12 minute scenario narration with quoted dialogue and transitions.

modules.title: Action and assessment
modules.purpose: Create an evidence-safe implementation brief and complete the knowledge check.
modules.voice_test: Produce a 10-12 minute assessment narration with questions and answer pauses.

interactive_prompts: Explain identity proofing in plain English.
What is the difference between identity, authority and consent?
What evidence would be needed to test the working hypothesis?
Give me a realistic executive scenario.
I got that wrong. Teach the concept again without giving me the answer first.
